doctrine: Geo-Economics & Full Spectrum Deterrence — Pakistan seeks to transition from purely geostrategic security rent-seeking to a connectivity-driven geo-economic transit hub bridging Central Asia, China, and the Middle East, while maintaining an unyielding Full Spectrum Nuclear Deterrent against conventional military pre-emption from India.
strategic_priorities: Deter Indian conventional and sub-conventional military pre-emption across the Line of Control through modern air, naval, and nuclear forces
Consolidate Phase II of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), expanding industrial parks, agricultural cooperation, and the deepwater port of Gwadar
Neutralize cross-border insurgent sanctuaries in Afghanistan (TTP) and secure border fencing along the Durand Line
Secure sovereign debt rollovers and multi-billion-dollar foreign direct investments from traditional Gulf allies (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar)
Maintain balanced pragmatic ties with the United States in counter-terrorism, climate resilience, and bilateral trade while deepening strategic integration with China
priority_regions: South Asia (India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Maldives — managing regional balance and multilateral SAARC revitalization)
East Asia (China — all-weather strategic cooperative partnership and core defense technology supplier)
Middle East & Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran — energy supplies, expatriate remittances, Islamic solidarity)
Central Asia & Afghanistan (CASA-1000 power project, TAPI gas pipeline, Trans-Afghan Railway trade connectivity)

cooperates_closely_with: China ('All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partner', primary defense technology provider, CPEC financier)
Turkey (comprehensive military partnership, naval corvettes [MILGEM / Babur class], joint aviation and drone programs)
Saudi Arabia & UAE (vital financial lifelines, central bank deposit support, deferred oil facilities, home to millions of diaspora workers)
Qatar (long-term liquefied natural gas supplier and sovereign investor)
United States (crucial export market, counter-terrorism dialogue, and key interlocutor within the IMF and multilateral lenders)
competes_or_disputes_with: India (core historical adversary over Kashmir, water distribution, border militarization, and competing regional alliances)
Taliban Administration in Afghanistan (frictions over the Durand Line border fencing and sheltering of anti-Pakistan TTP militants)
Regional insurgent factions (Baloch Liberation Army [BLA], Islamic State Khorasan Province [ISKP])
cooperation_and_competition.notes: Pakistan's strategic environment is shaped by its geographical location between nuclear-armed India, war-torn Afghanistan, energy-rich Iran, and rising superpower China. Islamabad strives to avoid being drawn into bloc rivalries between Washington and Beijing, emphasizing trade transit and bilateral defense diplomacy.

_meta.data_quality: sourced/analytical synthesis based on Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, National Security Policy (NSP) documents, and defense white papers
